name: Togo

facts.religion: Christian about 45%, Muslim about 20%, traditional faiths

system_note: A 2024 constitution moved power to a President of the Council, a post with no term limits.
snapshot: Faure Gnassingbé, whose family has ruled since 1967, switched to a parliamentary system that lets him stay in charge indefinitely as President of the Council.
culture: Togo shares Vodun traditions with neighbouring Benin, and Lomé's Akodessewa fetish market sells ingredients for traditional healing. The Ewe in the south and the Kabye in the north are the largest groups. Togolese footballer Emmanuel Adebayor became a national icon. French is official, with Ewe and Kabye taught in schools.
society: The deep-water port of Lomé is one of West Africa's busiest and a hub for landlocked Sahel countries. Phosphates and cotton are key exports. The Gnassingbé family has held power for nearly six decades. Jihadist attacks have reached the northern Savanes region.
situation: A new constitution adopted in 2024 made the president largely ceremonial and created the post of President of the Council of Ministers, chosen by the majority party. Gnassingbé took that post in May 2025. Protests in June 2025 against the change and against rising prices were met with force.
power: A parliamentary system under the 2024 constitution: the majority party in parliament chooses the President of the Council of Ministers, who holds executive power with no term limit, and the president is ceremonial. Gnassingbé's UNIR party dominates parliament.

leaders.state: President of the Council Faure Gnassingbé, in power since 2005
leaders.gov: Ceremonial President Jean-Lucien Savi de Tové

conflicts.name: Jihadist spillover into coastal West Africa (Benin, Togo)
